items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: The interviewee does not speak in the provided context. The mention of Lionel Hampton is made by the Interviewer, who recounts a story about Benny Goodman and Tommy Newsom. The interviewee's response ('Yeah, I always play...') does not address or confirm any personal relationship with Lionel Hampton

ctx.x: Oh, he made him put the money on the drummer.

Oh, he said he just got — Lionel Hampton said if you have any trouble with Benny, just get weirder than he is. And he did that, and I guess it worked for him at the time. Anyway, everybody’s got Benny stories. So you guys were kind of through the years have been alternating between big bands and combos and some studio work.

Yeah, I always play even, well Tommy was with the Tonight Show before I was. He was there with Skitch Henderson and Milton DeLugg. I started when Doc Severinsen started in 1967. But I always went right from there down and played someplace else. If it wasn’t the Half Note it was the Roosevelt Grill or something or the Plaza Nine. There was always some clubs.
